title: The Book of Joel Timeline
sub: The Locust Plague · I Will Pour Out My Spirit on All Flesh
desc: A devastating locust plague becomes an image of the coming Day of the LORD, met by a call to genuine repentance, and containing the Spirit-outpouring prophecy Peter quotes directly to explain the day of Pentecost.

eras.label: Era One · Joel 1
eras.name: The Locust Plague — a Nation Without Number
eras.dates: A devastating locust plague, described in waves eating what the last wave left, becomes the occasion for a call to lament. (This book's chapter divisions follow the Hebrew text, which has four chapters; most English translations combine the Hebrew's third and fourth chapters into one chapter 3, so references here may fall one chapter number higher than in an English Bible — a versification difference only, marked inline in the NET text itself.)

events.title: What the Locust Left, the Locust Consumed
events.detail: Four successive waves of locusts strip the land bare of grain, wine, and oil, an unprecedented disaster Joel says will be told to children's children for generations.

verses.text: “What the gazam-locust left the ‘arbeh-locust consumed; what the ‘arbeh-locust left the yeleq-locust consumed; and what the yeleq-locust left the hasil-locust consumed.”

events.title: The Day of the LORD Is Near — Destruction From the Almighty
events.detail: The locust plague itself becomes a sign pointing toward something worse still coming — the Day of the LORD, described as devastation from the Almighty, calling priests and people alike to a fast and a sacred assembly.

verses.text: “How awful that day will be! For the day of the LORD [Yahweh] is near; it will come as destruction from the Almighty [Shaddai].”

eras.label: Era Two · Joel 2
eras.name: An Army Like No Other — Tear Your Hearts, Not Your Garments
eras.dates: The locust imagery escalates into a military invasion so devastating it darkens the sun, met by one of the Old Testament's clearest calls to genuine repentance

events.title: A Huge and Powerful Army — There Has Never Been Anything Like It
events.detail: An invading army, described with the same locust imagery as chapter 1 but now unmistakably military, advances like fire through Eden itself, leaving desolate wilderness behind, while the LORD's own voice thunders at its head.

verses.text: “It will be a day of dreadful darkness… a huge and powerful army—there has never been anything like it ever before.”

events.title: Tear Your Hearts, Not Your Garments — the LORD Restores What the Locust Ate
events.detail: A call to genuine, internal repentance rather than mere outward ritual is met with compassion — the LORD becomes zealous for his land and promises to restore the years the locusts consumed with abundant grain, wine, and oil.

verses.text: “Tear your hearts, not just your garments.” Return to the LORD [Yahweh] your God [Elohim], for he is merciful and compassionate, slow to anger and boundless in loyal love.

eras.label: Era Three · Joel 3
eras.name: I Will Pour Out My Spirit on All Flesh
eras.dates: A short but pivotal five-verse promise, later quoted directly by Peter on the day of Pentecost as being fulfilled. (Numbered 2:28-32 in most English translations, marked inline in the NET text as “(3:1)”.)

events.title: Your Sons and Daughters Will Prophesy — Everyone Who Calls on the Name of the LORD
events.detail: The LORD promises to pour out his Spirit on all kinds of people, regardless of age, gender, or status, before the great and terrible Day of the LORD, ending in a promise of deliverance for everyone who calls on his name — the very passage Peter quotes in Acts 2 to explain Pentecost.

verses.text: “After all of this I will pour out my Spirit on all kinds of people. Your sons and daughters will prophesy. Your elderly will have prophetic dreams; your young men will see visions.”
“Everyone who calls on the name of the LORD [Yahweh] will be delivered… the remnant will be those whom the LORD [Yahweh] will call.” (Numbered 2:32 in most English translations.)

eras.label: Era Four · Joel 4
eras.name: The Valley of Jehoshaphat — the LORD Roars From Zion
eras.dates: A closing judgment oracle against the nations who scattered Israel, ending in a promise of Judah's permanent security. (Numbered chapter 3 in most English translations, marked inline in the NET text as “(4:1)”.)

events.title: The Valley of Decision — Beat Your Plowshares Into Swords
events.detail: The nations who scattered Israel and traded its children for wine are summoned to the Valley of Jehoshaphat for judgment, in a scene where the LORD's harvest-and-winepress imagery of judgment culminates in his voice roaring from Zion.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] roars from Zion; from Jerusalem his voice bellows out… the LORD [Yahweh] is a refuge for his people; he is a stronghold for the citizens of Israel.”

events.title: Judah Will Reside Securely Forever
events.detail: The book closes with a vision of restored fertility — mountains dripping with sweet wine — and a promise that Judah and Jerusalem will be secure from one generation to the next, in contrast to Egypt and Edom's coming desolation.

verses.text: “Judah will reside securely forever, and Jerusalem will be secure from one generation to the next.”
